title: Attention Is All You Need (test fixture)

vocabulary.definition: A discrete unit of input — typically a word piece or subword id the model operates on.
A learned dense vector that maps a token id into the model's continuous representation space.
A mechanism where every token attends to every other token via learned query, key, and value projections.
Three projections of each token used by attention: queries are matched against keys to produce weights that combine values.

sections.title: Problem
sections.summary: RNNs and CNNs were the dominant architectures for sequence modeling, but they struggled with long-range dependencies and forced sequential computation. The authors propose attention as the sole mechanism, removing recurrence entirely.
sections.mermaid:
flowchart LR

  Encoder --> Decoder
  Decoder -->|tokens| Output

import numpy as np
# Tokens as integer ids — the model never sees raw text.
tokens = np.array([1, 5, 3, 7])
print('shape:', tokens.shape)

sections.title: Self-attention
sections.summary: Each token attends to all others through learned query, key, and value projections. The dot-product attention formula scales by sqrt(d_k) for numerical stability before the softmax.
sections.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Q[Query] --> Score
  K[Key] --> Score
  Score -->|softmax| Weights
  V[Value] --> Output
  Weights --> Output
sections.code:
import numpy as np
d_k = 4
Q = np.random.randn(3, d_k); K = np.random.randn(3, d_k); V = np.random.randn(3, d_k)
scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d_k)
weights = np.exp(scores) / np.exp(scores).sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
print('attn out:\n', weights @ V)
